relevance_note: Case report of a mother and son with adult-onset Alexander disease carrying the same GFAP variant: "This mother-son pair with AD illustrates phenotypic variability from the same mutation within a single family."
method_note: Read the whole paper and wrote all values by hand (a short Python script only assembled the JSON). Labels 'Case 1' and 'Case 2' follow the section headings (the text also writes 'case 1'). is_proband left null: neither person is called proband or index case and the paper has two patients. Variant printed as 'pY242N' (Case 1 text, Case 2 text) and 'Y242N' (abstract, Discussion); recorded as printed, no cDNA or transcript given. Variant type not stated for this variant (the Discussion's 'single missense mutations' is about GFAP variants in general), so 'not reported'. Case 2 inheritance recorded as inherited maternal because the paper states his variant is the same substitution as observed in his mother (Case 1); the father is not mentioned. Case 1 parents not tested; inheritance not reported. Contradiction for Case 2: 'had no clear developmental abnormalities from birth' vs 'was only able to pull himself up to stand after 1 year of age' and a diagnosis at age 20 of 'a developmental disorder'; both rows emitted and checklist 'developmental delay' set to not reported. Case 1 checklist 'developmental delay' set excluded from 'no clear developmental abnormalities from birth' (hedged with 'clear'). Case 1 'Muscle weakness was observed' does not name the limbs, so checklist 'limb weakness' left not reported. Case 1 earlier diagnoses of spinocerebellar ataxia and MSA cerebellar type were revised and no ataxia is stated on her examination, so 'ataxia or cerebellar signs' left not reported (cerebellar atrophy on MRI and gaze-direction nystagmus recorded as features only). Case 2 checklist 'spasticity or pyramidal signs' observed from enhanced lower-limb deep tendon reflexes; the paper also states no pathological reflex in upper or lower limbs (recorded as excluded feature). Palatal myoclonus treated as palatal tremor for the checklist. Case 1 age at diagnosis of Alexander disease not stated (genetic diagnosis after admission in August 2014, age not given). Case 2 age at onset not recorded: the paper gives delayed standing after 1 year, poor exercise from high school and symptoms at 35 but does not name an onset. Country not stated for either patient (author affiliation in Japan only). Figure 1 legend (D) says 'with no remarkable changes', unclear meaning; not used.
